A six-parameter rigid body transformation (three rotations, three translations) was used for image realignment. The realigned datasets were normalized to the Talairach frame with a 12-parameters affine transformation ( ), using a voxel size of 3×3×3 mm 3 . Functional regions of interest (ROIs) with a volume of 729 mm 3 (cubic, 27 voxels) were defined at signal maxima and the average BOLD responses (% signal change) calculated for the a priori ROIs [rostro-ventral anterior cingulate cortex/medial orbitofrontal cortex (rACC/mOFC) and caudal–dorsal anterior cingulate cortex (cdACC)].

footer.value: Local maxima are listed for A: task activations (all words>baseline), B: hypoactivations (all words<baseline), and for whole brain correlations with C: performance accuracy (drug>neutral) and D: drug valence ratings (drug>baseline). A threshold of P <0.05 family-wise corrected was used for the main task activations/hypoactivations ( t -tests); P <0.01 uncorrected was used for all voxel-wise whole brain correlations; minimum cluster size was 50 contiguous voxels, 1.35 cc. Brodmann’s areas (BA), side (hemisphere), size (number of voxels), t values, P values (cluster level corrected) and Talairach coordinates are listed. All ACC/mOFC regions are shaded. ACC, anterior cingulate cortex; mOFC, medial orbitofrontal cortex.
